P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged with nothing read back — 'he gave me, like, a head start on you, so I kind of already know a little bit' — and the prospect could not initially remember who she had spoken to. Frame was two-part plus alignment, missing what's in the way and what you need. Agreement checked with 'Alrighty?' and answered 'Sounds good.' Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Age was asked properly, which is rare in this batch — 'How old are you as well? My mom would hate me to ask' — but height and weight never were. Occupation was volunteered mid-answer and the rep only returned to it later as a lead-in to the tax pitch. Diet was asked and explored well. The failure is the injury check, and it is the most consequential single omission in the batch: in her very first answer she said she tore her labrum and her ATFL in December, and no follow-up was ever asked — not which labrum, not whether it was surgical, not what her current restrictions are, not how her rehabilitation is going, and not whether her physical therapist would clear loaded overhead work. She mentioned the ongoing physical therapy a second time while scheduling and it still drew no question. No health-conditions question at all. Sleep and energy never raised.

P3.evidence: The best goals work in the batch. The six-month question ran cleanly and produced concrete function targets — carrying luggage without asking for help, holding posture after a day's work, walking stairs without getting winded. The feel-versus-look fork ran and was correctly resolved: 'it sounds like it's more about how you feel than how you look. It sounds like the look is a plus one of how you feel for you' — confirmed. Two strong reflect-backs, including 'this is more than kettlebells, it sounds like this is just you being the best you can be' and a full summary at 00:18:01 answered 'Yep, exactly.' What is missing is the bridge question and anyone else's stake. Her partner appears four separate times — motivating the household to eat well, calling her after the marathon PR — and was never once turned into a reason.

P4.evidence: The weakest fit between script and prospect on this call, and partly for legitimate reasons — she has no adherence problem to diagnose. She runs consistently, attends physical therapy weekly and describes herself as a yes woman. Past attempts were touched on through the physical therapy story and she named her own gap unprompted: 'I want to be with a professional person who understands kettlebells, and the technique, and the form.' But the rep never tested whether technique is genuinely the gap, never asked what has stopped her strength training sticking before, and never ran the root-cause reframe. For a prospect whose real constraint is time and integration with marathon training, that was the conversation to have.

P5.evidence: Never ran. She had supplied the material herself — worry about stress fractures in ageing female runners, 'life is so short, we could all die tomorrow', and a period of poor work-life balance she blames for the change in her body — and none of it was converted into a consequence frame. The call closed anyway on enthusiasm, which is exactly the pattern the scoring guidance warns about: the outcome does not redeem the phase.

P6.evidence: No commitment check ran before the offer. Belief was never tested and the all-in question was never asked. What stood in for it was enthusiasm — 'How do you feel about it all?' answered 'I'm excited to like just try and see where my body will go.' That is willingness to experiment, not a commitment, and the distinction matters for a prospect who describes herself as someone who will try anything once.

P11.evidence: The first two steps ran well. Payment was collected on the call and the recording was stopped to protect card details. The onboarding call with Trevor was booked for Wednesday 3:15pm Pacific, negotiated carefully around her physical therapy appointment and a South Bay commute, and her email was verified twice. The last two steps did not run: no agreement email, nothing signed on the call, no welcome email, no Skool community link and no onboarding questionnaire. This is now the same P11c and P11d gap on every closed call in the batch.

objection_plays.detail: The documented clinical script gap, and the most serious instance of it in this batch. The prospect raised injury risk herself in her opening answer — 'I want to do that, but not hurt myself' — in the same breath as disclosing a torn labrum and a torn ATFL, and she is in ongoing physical therapy with a clinician she trusts and quotes. There is no scripted play for routing a prospect toward clinical clearance, and none was improvised. What ran instead was reassurance and then a guarantee, 'we make sure that won't happen again', followed by a description of a first circuit of swings into snatches. The correct move — asking what her physical therapist would say about loaded overhead ballistic work, and making that the next step — was available all call and never taken. The playbook needs this play, and it needs it to be mandatory when an injury inside twelve months is disclosed.

A soft money signal appeared three times — 'I do have to see if I have that kind of money', 'I don't love blasting my card', and 'I just want to space out my credit card charges'. No isolation question and no permission-to-discuss-finances question. One financial-picture-adjacent question was asked, 'Do you have a business?', but as a lead-in to the tax pitch rather than as a diagnostic. She resolved it herself by proposing $3,000 now and $3,000 later. The rep held the price without discounting, which is the right outcome, but it was reached by the prospect rather than by the play.

notes: Excellent goals work and a clean close, on the best-qualified prospect in the batch — and the baseline phase failed in the one place it could not afford to. A labral tear and an ATFL tear disclosed at ninety seconds drew zero follow-up questions across forty-five minutes, and the only time the injury was mentioned again was to promise it would not recur. Coach one rule above everything else here: any injury disclosed within the last twelve months triggers a full injury sub-interview and a clearance question before any close is attempted, regardless of how well the call is going.
